summary: The pnpm repository holds two package managers at once. pnpm11 is the TypeScript v11 CLI, split into many small packages grouped by concern. pnpm is the Rust v12 rewrite, an 88-crate workspace where new features now land. pnpr is a separate Rust server that resolves dependencies remotely, and .changeset carries the release notes for all of it.

districts.name: The New Foundry
districts.purpose: The Rust v12 CLI (pacquet): an 88-crate workspace covering resolution, the store, lockfiles, workspaces and the command surface.

districts.name: The Old Works
districts.purpose: The TypeScript v11 CLI, kept for bug fixes only, grouped into installing, deps, resolving, lockfile, store, workspace and cli packages.

districts.name: The Remote Depot
districts.purpose: A Rust server that resolves a project's dependencies server-side and streams back a lockfile, with a TypeScript client beside it.

districts.name: The Records Office
districts.purpose: Several hundred pending changeset files, one per change, which assemble into the release notes and version bumps.

districts.name: Civic Offices
districts.purpose: Fifty-plus workflow and config files: CI, benchmarks, ecosystem end-to-end runs, security audit, Docker images and release PRs.

districts.name: The Patchworks
districts.purpose: Patched dependencies applied through pnpm's own patch mechanism, dogfooding the feature.

districts.name: The Container Yard
districts.purpose: The published Docker images for running pnpm in CI.

importantModules.role: The Rust v12 workspace: 88 crates covering the command surface, config, resolvers, registry and network, the content-addressable store, lockfiles and hoisting.
The v11 install pipeline: client, context, dependency installer and resolver packages.
The pnpr server crates: registry routes, upstream proxying, storage, policy, OSV advisories, OCI artifacts and per-ecosystem resolvers.
The v11 dependency-graph packages: graph builder, hasher and sequencer, dependency paths, peer ranges, list and why inspection, security audit and status.
The Rust workspace root: its members are pnpm/crates/*, pnpm/tasks/* and pnpr/crates/*, and every internal crate path and shared dependency is pinned here.
The v11 resolvers, one package per specifier kind: npm, git, jsr, local and tarball, over a shared resolver base.
The v11 workspace packages: root finding, project and manifest readers and writers, the projects graph, filter and sorter, task scheduler and workspace state.
The v11 settings packages: the config reader and writer, override parsing, registry normalisation and per-package selection, auth keys and version policy.
The v11 lockfile packages: filesystem access, merging, pruning, verification, preferred versions, dedicated lockfiles and the walker.
The published v11 package: the pnpm.cjs entry that is still the binary for the TypeScript line, the bundling scripts, the node-gyp bins and its own tests.
The v11 execution packages: the exec and run commands, npm lifecycle script running, package preparation and the CLI runner child processes go through.
The v11 content-addressable store: cafs, the store controller and the connection manager the install pipeline talks to.
The v11 hashing packages: content hashes, integrity strings, a stable object hasher and the shasums file reader.
The v11 command line: argument parsing, the command registry and its metadata, the shared option help text and the default reporter.
Internal v11 development packages: shared tsconfig, eslint and jest config, temp directory and fixture preparation, and the project and store test assertions.
The v11 release side: the deploy, pack and publish commands, the exportable manifest written into a published tarball, and version bumping.
The v11 filesystem packages: hard-linking a package out of the store into node_modules, symlinking dependencies, packlists and reading modules directories.
The cargo-equivalence task: it resolves real Cargo workspaces with both cargo and pnpm v12 and diffs the lockfiles, because v12 reimplements cargo's resolver.
The v11 fetchers, one per source: tarball, git, directory and binary, over a shared fetcher base, with the picker that chooses between them.
The v11 build step: deciding which packages require a build, the policy that approves them, and running builds during and after an install.
Design notes for in-flight v12 work: ecosystem install, lockfile resolution reuse, multi-level hoisting, the napi bindings, a Python spike and test porting.
The v11 binary handling: resolving a package's bin entries, linking them into node_modules/.bin through cmd shims, and removing them again.
The v11 engine packages: pnpm setup and self-update, the with command, and the resolvers for the Node, Deno and Bun runtimes a project pins.
The npm packaging for the Rust CLI: the pnpm, pnpx, pn and pnx bin shims, the installer that fetches the right platform binary, and the napi package.
The TypeScript client for the pnpr server: posts a project's dependencies and lockfile, reads the streamed reply and returns a lockfile for a headless install.
Several hundred fixture projects the v11 suites install against: circular deps, outdated and deprecated deps, custom modules dirs and missing lockfiles.
The v11 network packages: the fetch wrapper, per-registry auth headers, browser-based web login and the git helpers the git fetcher calls.

strengths: The Rust workspace is cut into narrow crates named after what they do, so resolution, store, lockfile and workspace concerns never blur into one another.
The rewrite is staged in the open: pnpm/README.md states which version gets features, which gets fixes, and how bugs in both are handled.
A cargo-equivalence workflow exists to compare the two implementations rather than trusting that the rewrite behaves the same.
Releases are assembled from per-change changesets instead of a hand-edited changelog.
CI is unusually broad for a package manager: benchmarks, ecosystem end-to-end runs, security audit and Docker publishing all run from this repository.
concerns: Two complete implementations of the same tool live side by side, so a bug present in both has to be fixed twice in two languages.
Nearly 1,100 open issues and pull requests sit against the repository, which is a lot of surface for a tool in the middle of a rewrite.
Around 550 pending changeset files suggests releases batch a great deal of change at once.
Eighty-eight crates plus the v11 package set is a lot of top-level vocabulary before a newcomer can find where an install actually starts.
Contributors need both a Rust toolchain and a Node toolchain before either half of the repository builds.
